title: Coefficient transport of adjunction exchange
statement: In eight categories with four specified adjunctions, two horizontal squares and two coefficient squares, let B and Be satisfy the exchange counit equations. Let the vertical pull coefficient comparisons be invertible and the horizontal comparisons be natural transformations. Let the two push comparisons satisfy their counit mate equations. If the pull-comparison cube commutes, the displayed square between the two exchange maps and the push comparisons commutes. No exchange map is assumed invertible.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Remark 6.8.15; explicit formal coefficient and adjunction argument

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the target second adjunction inverse Hom equivalence to the desired equation.

Expand each exchange adjunct using its counit equation. Naturality moves the push comparison through the target square, and its mate equation replaces it. Naturality of the target counit and the second push mate equation rewrite the other side.

Use inverse pull naturality and the source exchange adjunct equation. After naturality of the remaining horizontal comparison, precompose and postcompose the pull-comparison cube by inverse pull comparisons and cancel the isomorphisms. This yields equality of the adjuncts. The calculation uses the cube only at R.obj K; the pointwise API exposes this weaker requirement, and the original theorem applies it to the universally given cube.

    (θ : G ⋙ V ⟶ U ⋙ H) (θe : Ge ⋙ Ve ⟶ Ue ⋙ He)

    (αU : U ⋙ T₂ ≅ T₁ ⋙ Ue) (αV : V ⋙ T₄ ≅ T₃ ⋙ Ve)
    (αG : G ⋙ T₃ ⟶ T₁ ⋙ Ge) (αH : H ⋙ T₄ ⟶ T₂ ⋙ He)
    (δ : R ⋙ T₁ ⟶ T₂ ⋙ Re) (δ' : S ⋙ T₃ ⟶ T₄ ⋙ Se)
    (hδ : ∀ K, Ue.map (δ.app K) ≫ ae.counit.app (T₂.obj K) =
      αU.inv.app (R.obj K) ≫ T₂.map (a.counit.app K))

    (hcube : ∀ K, T₄.map (θ.app K) ≫ αH.app (U.obj K) ≫
        He.map (αU.hom.app K) =
      αV.hom.app (G.obj K) ≫ Ve.map (αG.app K) ≫ θe.app (T₁.obj K))
    (K : C₂) :
    αG.app (R.obj K) ≫ Ge.map (δ.app K) ≫ Be.app (T₂.obj K) =
      T₃.map (B.app K) ≫ δ'.app (H.obj K) ≫ Se.map (αH.app K)
